assumptions: Compounds annually using your annual return input.
Monthly income uses an illustrative 4% annual withdrawal estimate divided by 12.
Taxes, fees, IRS limits, vesting rules, loans, and withdrawals are not modeled.
disclaimer: This calculator does not provide financial, investment, tax, or legal advice.
Results are hypothetical and not guaranteed.

projection.label: Projection table
projection.title: Balance over time
projection.description: Year-by-year estimate based on the current inputs.

formula.label: Plain-English method
formula.title: 401(k) formula and assumptions
formula.description: This calculator projects one year at a time. For each projected year, salary is increased first, then employee contributions and employer match are added after applying the annual return assumption to the existing balance.
lines: employee contribution = salary × employee contribution percent
eligible match percent = min(employee contribution percent, match limit percent)
employer match = salary × eligible match percent × employer match percent
balance = balance × (1 + annual return) + employee contribution + employer match
formula.estimateDescription: Investment returns vary. Salary, contributions, employer match, fees, taxes, plan rules, and federal contribution limits may also change. Compare assumptions instead of treating one result as guaranteed.

steps.title: Enter age and retirement age
steps.description: The difference between these ages determines how many years are projected.

steps.title: Add balance and salary
steps.description: Your current balance is the starting point. Salary grows annually using your input.

steps.title: Set contribution and match
steps.description: Contribution, employer match, and match limit determine how much new money is added.

steps.title: Compare scenarios
steps.description: Adjust return, salary growth, and contribution assumptions to compare projections.

inputExplanations.label: Input explanations
inputExplanations.title: What each 401(k) input means

items.title: Employee contribution
items.description: The percent of salary you contribute to your 401(k). This estimate does not apply IRS annual contribution limits.

items.title: Employer match
items.description: The portion of eligible employee contributions your employer adds. A 50% match means $0.50 per eligible $1.00 contributed.

items.title: Match limit
items.description: The maximum salary percentage eligible for matching. If you contribute above the match limit, the extra contribution is not matched in this model.

items.title: Annual return
items.description: A hypothetical average annual return. Real markets do not move in a smooth line and may be higher or lower.

items.title: Salary increase
items.description: The assumed annual salary growth rate used before calculating each future year's contribution and employer match.

inputExplanations.reminderDescription: Small changes in salary growth, contribution rate, match, and return assumptions can produce very different long-term results. Compare scenarios before relying on one estimate.

trust.label: Trust and methodology
trust.title: Know what the estimate includes
trust.description: Review the calculation order, modeled assumptions, and known exclusions before relying on a projection.

items.question: What does this 401k Calculator estimate?
items.answer: It estimates a future 401(k) balance, employee contributions, employer match, investment growth, illustrative monthly retirement income, and a year-by-year projection.

items.question: Does this calculator store my financial information?
items.answer: No. The calculator runs locally in your browser and does not require login, account creation, or data submission.

items.question: How is employer match calculated?
items.answer: Employer match is salary multiplied by the lesser of your employee contribution percent and the match limit percent, then multiplied by the employer match percent.

items.question: Are the results guaranteed?
items.answer: No. Results are hypothetical estimates. Actual returns, salary changes, contribution limits, fees, taxes, and plan rules may differ.

items.question: Is this financial advice?
items.answer: No. This calculator is for educational purposes and does not provide financial, investment, tax, legal, or retirement planning advice.
